newsitem.title: USA: Wall St's Santa rally resumes ahead of Christmas.
newsitem.headline: Wall St's Santa rally resumes ahead of Christmas.

text.p: Wall Street's Santa Claus rally resumed as investors returned to the safety of blue chip names, but volume was very light in the abbreviated Christmas Eve trading session.

"It's the last day for Christmas shopping and the last day of trading before Christmas. We have a holiday environment with much of the tax-selling apparently behind us. Santa is surprising us again," said Alan Ackerman of Fahnestock & Co.
The Dow industrials rose 34 to about 6523, nearing its record closing high of 6547.79 set on November 25.
U.S. stock markets closed early at 1300 EST/1800 GMT. U.S. financial markets will be closed Wednesday, Christmas Day.
Winners outpaced losers 4-3 on NYSE volume of about 165 million shares.
The Nasdaq Composite surged eight to about 1288.
"The traditional Christmas rally is at hand," said Ackerman, a market strategist at Fahnestock.
The rally bode well for the Street's prospects according to the old saying -- "If Santa should fail to call, bears could come to Broad and Wall," site of the New York Stock Exchange.

As for Tuesday's Dow action, David Kelly, senior economist with Primark Decision Economics, said: "It's not a sign of people rooting out value in smaller companies, it's just money looking for a safe home."
A rebound in technology stocks helped to lead stocks higher. Compaq rose 1-7/8 to 74-5/8, Seagate added 2-1/8 to 40-1/8, IBM was up 1-3/4 to 155-7/8 and Intel rose 3-1/4 to 135-1/2.
Among individual stocks, Motorola rose 1-5/8 to 60-1/2. Lehman Brothers called Motorola the "best idea for 1997 in the wireless communications equipment industry."

KCS Energy rallied 7-7/8 to 37-5/8 after news that it settled all litigation with Tennessee Gas Pipeline. KCS said 1997 and 1998 earnings will suffer from the settlement that calls for the companies to end their contract two years ahead of schedule.
Digi International slumped 3-7/8 to 8-7/8 after warning first-quarter earnings will fall short of expectations.

TRO Learning stumbled 6-3/4 to 10-1/2. TRO said its fiscal 1996 fourth quarter revenues and profits fell short of expectations and that, as a result of the lower earnings, the company is in non-compliance with its loan agreement.

Matrix Pharmaceutical shed 2-3/8 to 6-1/8 after getting an action letter from the FDA identifying areas to resolve before the company's New Drug Applucation for AccuSite Injectable Gel can be approved. AccuSite is used to treat genital warts. Cowen cut Matrix to neutral from buy.
Day Runner lost 4-3/4 to 19-1/4 after forecasting a drop in second-quarter results.
The S&P 500 rose 4.11 to 751.03.
The Nasdaq Composite rose 8.11 to 1287.63.
(Figures official as of 1645 EST/2145 GMT).
The stock market is closed on December 25.
-- Wall Street desk 212 859 1721
